page_title: Cyberdog — Vos serveurs, une seule fenêtre.

sources.entry: Cyberdog - SSH and SFTP client with a built-in terminal, a server health dashboard and FTP, S3 and WebDAV support. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/pickywawa/cyberdog) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Cyberdog
summary.one_liner: Cyberdog is a free, open-source desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that combines a file explorer (SFTP and many cloud/storage protocols), an SSH terminal and a server health dashboard in one window.
use_cases: Transfer and sync files with remote servers over SFTP
Monitor CPU, memory, disks and processes on servers
Connect to servers through a bastion host
Manage SSH keys and install public keys on servers
Browse S3, WebDAV, FTP or cloud storage in one explorer
Import server configs from Cyberduck, FileZilla or WinSCP
summary.what_it_does: Cyberdog provides a dual-pane file explorer for SFTP/SSH, FTP/FTPS, S3-compatible storage, Azure, WebDAV, SMB and cloud drives such as Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive, with transfer queues, pause and resume. It includes an SSH terminal opened in the current folder and a server health view covering CPU, memory, disks, processes, systemd services, Docker containers and live logs. It also offers SSH key generation and fingerprint checks, SSL certificate expiry views, and a built-in editor for remote files. Servers can be grouped, imported from other clients, and reached through a bastion host with fingerprint verification.
notable: Open source under MIT license, with local tools free including team sharing and secrets vaults
Bastion host support with a second end-to-end SSH session and fingerprint checks
Imports configurations from Cyberduck, FileZilla and WinSCP
Connects to SSH servers without installing any agent on the server
caveats: Terminal, server health, Docker and logs only work with SSH servers
Windows builds are not yet code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn
SSL view only refreshes while the app is open and does not monitor servers when closed
Team sharing requires creating an account, and shared configurations are hosted on Supabase
